newsitem.title: UK: Sinn Fein urges IRA to restore truce-BBC.
newsitem.headline: Sinn Fein urges IRA to restore truce-BBC.

text.p: Sinn Fein's chief negotiator Martin McGuinness asked IRA guerrillas on Friday to restore a ceasefire that collapsed in February 1996, BBC radio reported.
The BBC said it was quoting from a statement issued by Sinn Fein just before 1400 GMT.
The statement was issued by McGuinness and Sinn Fein president Gerry Adams. They said they expected the IRA to respond positively to their request, the BBC said.
Earlier, Adams indicated in a joint statement with moderate nationalist leader John Hume that Britain had removed some obstacles to meaningful negotiations on the future of Northern Ireland.

Britain and Ireland, who are partners in a three-year peace initiative, say the Irish Republican Army must abandon violence for Sinn Fein to be given a place in all-party peace talks. Sinn Fein is the political wing of the IRA.

The IRA has waged a war for 28 years to end British rule and merge Northern Ireland with the neighbouring republic of Ireland. It declared a ceasefire in September 1994 but resumed armed hostilities in February 1996, saying it was frustrated that Britain had refused it a political voice in talks.
